environment: Windows 11 25H2 x64; Flutter 3.47.5; Dart 3.13.4; Visual Studio Build Tools 2022 17.14.41; Windows SDK 10.0.26100.0
scenario: Build the shared Flutter client as a portable Windows x64 bundle after the Android, iOS and shared-client updates on origin/master.

checks.name: Flutter analyzer
checks.observation: No application errors or warnings; two info-level diagnostics in the local flutter_webrtc package (unnecessary_library_name and invalid_runtime_check_with_js_interop_types) caused exit code 1.

checks.name: Windows Release compilation
checks.observation: MSVC built boohtacord_desktop.exe and the full Flutter bundle. The native flutter_soloud dependency emitted compiler warnings.

checks.name: Portable archive inventory and hash
checks.observation: The 34-entry archive includes boohtacord_desktop.exe, data/, Flutter and plugin DLLs, including libwebrtc.dll. All 32 files were decompressed and read successfully (58,239,579 uncompressed bytes).

checks.name: Windows native launch smoke
checks.observation: The compiled Release executable opened a BOOHTACORD window. The process was still running and responding after five seconds, then was stopped. No account login was attempted.

checks.name: Extracted ZIP runtime and media acceptance
checks.observation: The extracted-copy launch and cleanup attempt was rejected by automatic approval review. Login, voice, screen-sharing, and second-peer behavior were not observed.

remaining: Launch the extracted ZIP on Windows and verify session handling, voice, real screen/window capture, failure rollback, and a second peer before public release.
